about: Test cases for the action binding extension 0.3.0, over the values in vectors.json, which generate_vectors.py writes from the templates below (A0: an approved and executed payment; A1: a rejected one; both 0.3.0, unsigned, which the generator signs or copies as the vectors say) and the report template. Schema cases apply a patch to an attachment from the vectors or to base_report (an empty patch tests the base itself), so each negative case differs from a valid instance by the one thing it tests; C cases check the fixture records against the core decision-record schema in standard/v5.0. Vector cases recompute the vectors. Digest cases are as in 0.2.0. Binding cases run the reference check of one attachment's stages, with its decision record or without it (record null); every dimension is expected verified, and execution_state attempted, unless the case says otherwise. Signature cases run the reference check of one attachment's issuer signature, with the signatures attachment beside (beside, unless the case names another or none) and the policy, each patched; the attachment is the first covered (covers, default A0 and A1) unless index says otherwise. Pairing cases read base_report with the attachments it covers, the records in base_context, the attachment beside and the policy, which JSON Schema cannot do. An attachment's bytes as received are its JSON with no whitespace, in UTF-8 (json.dumps with separators (",", ":") and ensure_ascii False), except the texts, read as written. Patches name a value, a value from vectors.json (vector) or a document's digest (digest_of: attachment:<name> or beside). Specifications S0 to S5 and records R0 to R4 are synthetic; their bytes are the UTF-8 (here ASCII) encoding of each text, and the digests below also serve as simple vectors. S1, S2 and S3 change only the amount, the target and the destination of S0; S5 is S0 without its policy_version. R0 is affirmed and sealed: its seal_hash is the SHA-256 of R0 with the seal_hash value replaced by 64 zeros, as the repository's governance records are sealed. R2 is R1 with a review_log outcome word the check does not know. R3 is R0 with two reviewers in its review_log, and R4 is R0 with an affirmation time that has no offset; both are sealed the same way.
